takeaways.label: Music margin story delivered
takeaways.text: Music EBIT margin jumped 700 bps YoY to 55.4% as content bought 2–4 years ago now generates revenue far exceeding its charge-off, exactly the trajectory management predicted in FY24.

takeaways.label: Revenue growth on track, but evaluate on 12-month basis
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 37% YoY to ₹314.3 crore, yet management repeatedly asked investors to ignore quarterly swings and judge performance only on a rolling 12-month view.

takeaways.label: Content engine is scaling
takeaways.text: FY27 content spend guided at ₹300–350 crore, with ~₹1,200 crore planned over FY28–FY30; the 5-year payback model is now visibly converting into margin expansion.

takeaways.label: Video and events are deliberate drags
takeaways.text: Video revenue fell 16% as the film business is wound down, and live events posted a loss as the mix shifts from artist concerts to owned IPs, both conscious investments with future payoff promised.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the ~100 hours of AI-generated podcast content lands in Q3, any movement on short-format monetization shifting from fixed-fee to ad-share, and the pace of further music margin expansion as the content portfolio ages.

points.label: The lagged-content flywheel
points.text: Content investments made in FY24, FY25, and FY26 have reached the stage where the revenue increase from them is far higher than the cost charge-off. In the initial year of investment, the revenue bump was just equal to the charge-off, so the margin benefit is back-end loaded and now compounding.

points.label: Non-film content driving growth
points.text: H1 saw greater focus on non-film music including I-Pop Star albums in Hindi and Tamil, Haryanvi, Bihari, and Punjabi superstar Nijjar's album, which threw multiple trending songs on YouTube and Instagram. The biggest film hit was the Telugu album "Paradise," whose song 'yeshanagula' hit global #1 on YouTube's daily music video charts.

points.label: Paid subscription is the structural tailwind
points.text: Paid subscription is growing much faster than ad-based, and paid customers generate a much higher yield per stream than free customers. Spotify is calling India its biggest growth opportunity and is increasing ad load on the free tier to drive conversion to paid.

points.label: Pricing power is still years away
points.text: Pricing as a second growth engine is expected to start kicking in, hopefully, 2–3 years from now; currently growth comes only from new subscribers. Universal Music has agreed to a windowing concept in India where some content goes first to the paid side, a model Saregama is watching.

points.label: Short-format monetization stuck
points.text: Short-format apps like Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts remain on fixed-fee deals. Management wants a shift to share-of-advertising basis but it has not happened yet, and any change will be shared only when it occurs.

points.label: Non-digital revenue is a slow grind
points.text: On the non-digital side, only brand licensing and public performance are showing decent growth, while TV channels and radio stations are growing at a much slower pace.

quotes.text: Mehra: "We had stated this in financial year ‘24 itself, that as we started investing heavily in newer content, in the initial year when you invest in content, the bump in revenue was just equal to the charge-off that we were taking on the content cost. Some of those content investments that we made in financial year ‘24, ‘25 or ‘26 have now reached a stage whereby the revenue increase on account of them is far higher than the cost charge that we are taking."

points.label: FY27 spend
points.text: ₹300–350 crore guided for new content, with H2 film albums including Sanjay Leela Bhansali's "Love & War," Sivakarthikeyan's "Seyon," Dharma's Kartik Aaryan starrer "Naagzilla," and a Tiger Shroff movie produced by Bhansali.

points.label: FY28–FY30 trajectory
points.text: ~₹1,200 crore over three years, assuming a 10% per annum nominal increase from the FY27 midpoint of ₹325 crore. The 5-year payback period guidance is maintained for all new music, followed by 55–75 years of returns.

points.label: The math that makes it work
points.text: As content reaches year three or four, the charge-off becomes much smaller than the revenue it generates, contributing directly to margin. Quarter-to-quarter variation depends on timing of big releases and marketing cost booking, which is why management insists on a 12-month rolling view.

points.label: AI content team
points.text: A dedicated team is using GenAI tools to create adjacent audio content like podcasts using Saregama songs, and building new-age music videos around older songs. ~100 hours of podcast content is planned for Q3 release.

points.label: AI process team
points.text: A second AI-dedicated team is optimising internal processes, which has already resulted in marginal savings in manpower cost. Full impact of AI initiatives is expected to be visible over the next few quarters.

points.label: IP protection is active
points.text: All new digital licensing agreements are building protection against dilution of rights and potential fraud. The company has invested in technology to track AI cover versions on streaming platforms and either buys them out or pulls them down. It is also proactively opening dialogue with AI creators to own and distribute AI versions of its biggest songs.

points.label: Bullish but vigilant
points.text: Management sees AI as a tool that will help large IP owners, while being wary that nobody should be able to infringe content without a license. The stance is to support licensed innovation and consistently fight against unlicensed exploitation.

quotes.text: Mehra: "Saregama's position on AI remains that it will be beneficial to the company in the long run, both in terms of cost reduction and speed to market. But while we support licensed innovation, we at Saregama will consistently fight against unlicensed exploitation."

points.label: Video is shrinking by design
points.text: Revenue declined 16% to ₹18.3 crore because of a conscious decision to wind down the film business and invest in Bhansali Productions instead. Further decline is expected in coming quarters as the transition plays out. The company will continue investing in GenZ-focused short-format content and TV/web shows, most of which are low-ticket items with advertiser or platform commitment before shooting.

points.label: Bhansali Productions
points.text: Geared up for its biggest release "Love & War" in Q4 and actively working on a slate for FY28.

points.label: Live events loss
points.text: The loss this quarter stems from a conscious shift from artist-based concerts to IP-based events like UN40, HaHaKaar, Krishna, and Carvaan Live, where initial runs require higher investments that are charged off rather than capitalised. H1 events revenue of ₹61 crore was driven partly by a very successful Ilaiyaraaja US tour across 11 cities serving 20,000 audience members.

points.label: Diljit tour passed
points.text: Saregama is not doing the Diljit Dosanjh India tour this season because the financials were not working out. A Guru Randhawa show, UN40, HaHaKaar, and a tour by an artist described as bigger than mid-level are in the pipeline.

points.label: Pocket Aces
points.text: Reached break-even in FY26 and is moving towards profitability this year. Management declined to split its contribution within artist management, calling it a combined number.

points.label: Unallocable expenditure
points.text: The increase was driven by a 55% YoY decline in other income, which is netted against unallocable costs. QIP money that previously earned interest has been invested in Pocket Aces, Haryanvi catalog, and Bhansali. Excluding the other income impact, unallocable cost is flat versus last year.

points.label: A unique B2C asset
points.text: Management positions Saregama as the only music label globally with direct customer relationships, built through Carvaan hardware, live events, and now the Carvaan app. The strategy is to build an engaged community of middle-aged to older people connecting through music and entertainment, while younger audiences are targeted separately under FilterCopy or the Saregama brand.

points.label: Carvaan Live
points.text: The brand has been extended into smaller sit-down concerts targeting middle-aged and older audiences, with 54 shows produced in Q2. Devotional format shows featuring Manoj Muntashir's Krishna, Backstage Siblings, and Jaya Kishori added 17 shows.

points.label: Carvaan app
points.text: Still in test phase, with experimentation continuing through this financial year to understand what content works. There is no intention to make it a hardcore music streaming app; the aim is to build a community around older people. Details will be shared once the experimentation phase is over and the app starts being pushed in the market, in "another four to six months."

points.label: Carvaan Club
points.text: Hardware, live events, and the app are being combined under Carvaan Club. Monetization and engagement details will be shared after testing and customer experimentation conclude, with management asking investors to "give us until the end of the year."

quotes.text: Mehra: "We happen to be the only music label, not just in India but globally, which has direct customer relationships. It's the Carvaan part which came out very, very handy for us. So now, we are the only label that has got hardware. We are the only label that is also selling live events. So everybody else has a B2B relationship. We also have a B2C relationship."

items.title: Music margin cycle
items.text: Management guides the music vertical to 20-23% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years with 60-65% EBITDA margins; music EBITDA margin already rose 700bps YoY to 55.4% in Q2 FY27 as FY24-FY26 content passes its ~5-year payback. With ₹1,000 crore invested across FY25-FY27 and spend growth slowing to 6-10% from FY28, revenue keeps compounding while content costs flatten - the flagged profit-growth cycle is underway.

items.title: Bhansali Productions stake
items.text: Saregama completed a ₹325 crore first tranche for 28% of Bhansali Productions in January 2026, with options to reach 49.9% on performance and 51% by 2030 at no further committed cost. BPPL exclusively sells all future film music to Saregama on a pre-agreed formula - 30-40% of future Hindi film acquisitions, securing A and B+ albums for 24-30 months - and the stake turned EPS-accretive, contributing ₹3.99 crore in Q2 FY27.

items.title: Paid subscription take-off
items.text: India's paid music penetration is under 3% of internet users vs 57% in the US, and platforms like Spotify are pushing paid conversion, with Universal already windowing new content behind paywalls. Management says the 20-23% music growth guidance assumes no subscription take-off - if leading platforms shut free tiers, subscription revenue could "literally double" YoY, expected within 1-3 years.

items.title: Live events scale-up
items.text: Live events revenue doubled YoY to ₹44.7 crore in Q2 FY27 across concerts, devotional, stand-up and experiential formats, with a Dubai subsidiary incorporated for Middle East expansion. The vertical is capital-light - ~₹15 crore of assets rotating in 30-40 days - targeting high single-digit margins over 2-3 years and seen by management as potentially the fastest-growing vertical.

items.title: Artist management build-out
items.text: The roster reached 340 artists with 45 crore+ combined followers at Q2 FY27, and H1 FY27 artist management revenue grew almost 100%, running at ~₹40 crore per quarter with ~10% EBITDA margins. Pocket Aces reached breakeven in FY26 as promised and is expected to grow at 25% CAGR, while its Finnet acquisition (November 2025) adds influencer marketing capability.

items.title: AI content and cost levers
items.text: Around 100 hours of AI-created podcast content releases in Q3 FY27, and GenAI music videos for the classic catalogue cut production from 10-12 days to under 3 - heading to 1-1.5 days - at costs as low as ₹70,000 with ~1-year payback. This monetises the 20th-century catalogue's missing music videos, a gap no competitor of similar scale faces.

items.title: Regional and Punjabi push
items.text: After two failed attempts, a new Punjabi model bundling recorded music with live events is underway, with a performance update expected by end-Q3 FY27. The NAV Records acquisition made Saregama the Haryanvi leader, and FY26's ₹105 crore of catalogue purchases - the highest ever - extend regional depth.
